name: AnimatedBeam
description: A light that travels along a curved line between two elements, such as two cards in a diagram. The line is drawn on a canvas that fills the container, so nothing is added to the accessibility tree.

containerRef.description: Ref of the positioned element that holds both endpoints.

fromRef.description: Ref of the element the line starts at. Use this or fromId.

toRef.description: Ref of the element the line ends at. Use this or toId.

fromId.description: The id of the start element, when a ref is not handy.

toId.description: The id of the end element, when a ref is not handy.

curvature.description: How far the line bows away from a straight one, in pixels. Negative bows the other way.

reverse.description: The light travels from the end to the start.

duration.description: Seconds for the light to cross.

pathColor.description: Colour of the resting line, any CSS colour. Defaults to the border colour.

beamColor.description: Colour of the travelling light, any CSS colour. Defaults to the primary action colour.

isPaused.description: Stops the effect and shows it still.

requirements: Decoration only: the effect is aria-hidden, never takes focus and never blocks the pointer
Stands still for visitors who ask for less motion (prefers-reduced-motion) and inside an rdm-still container, and isPaused stops it too
Does not flash: nothing changes more than three times in a second (WCAG 2.3.1)
The resting line stays visible when the light is still, so the connection is never lost
The connection must also be stated in text near the diagram: the line alone says nothing to a screen reader
In forced-colors (high contrast) mode the canvas is hidden
Redraws when the container or an endpoint changes size, and is paused while off-screen
screenReader: Not announced: the canvas is hidden from assistive technology

use_when: A flow between two or three boxes in a diagram
Showing that two services are connected
avoid_when: Carrying meaning that is not also written down
Many lines that all move at once
anti_patterns: Relying on the line to explain the relationship
Leaving the container without position: relative, so the canvas escapes it
